title: Collect-request scam
tagline: A buyer says: just accept and enter your PIN to receive money.
intro: You listed an old phone on a second-hand marketplace. {{name}} replies within minutes and says a payment of ₹{{amount}} is on the way. Your {{app}} app now shows a request. What do you do?

name: Rohit
Meera
Karan
Ananya
Imran
Divya
wording: I'm travelling, so a friend will collect it.
I've already paid the delivery person.
I'm buying it as a gift.

payloadTemplate.body: Hi! I'll buy your item right now at full price, no bargaining. {{wording}} I'm sending a payment request of ₹{{amount}}. Just accept it and enter your UPI PIN to receive the money. I can't talk on a call, only chat. Do it urgently or I'll buy from someone else!

steps.label: Spot the red flags in the buyer's message
steps.cue: Inspect the buyer's message first to spot manipulation cues before acting.
steps.explanation: Scam messages use pressure, secrecy and odd requests. Spotting them early keeps you calm and in control.

steps.label: Open {{app}} yourself
steps.cue: Verify any payment claim directly inside your own payment app, never through chat.
steps.explanation: Go to your payment app directly. You can then see the real request and its details instead of trusting what a message says.

steps.label: Decline the collect request
steps.cue: Remember: receiving money never requires approving a collect request or entering a PIN.
steps.explanation: Approving a collect request sends money out of your account. Declining it is the safe choice. Receiving money never needs your approval.

steps.label: Check your balance and history
steps.cue: Confirm your account activity so you know for sure no money was debited.
steps.explanation: A quick check confirms that nothing was debited and helps you notice anything odd straight away.

steps.label: Block and report the sender's UPI ID
steps.cue: Stop repeat requests from this sender and flag the ID to help protect others.
steps.explanation: Blocking stops more requests from that ID. Reporting helps protect other people too.

distractors.label: Reply to the buyer and agree
distractors.explanation: Replying tells a scammer that you are active and easy to pressure. Do not chat further with someone who pushes you.

distractors.label: Approve the request
distractors.explanation: Approving a collect request means you are paying, not receiving. The next screen would ask for your PIN.

distractors.label: Send money to a contact
distractors.explanation: Sending money does not cancel or fix anything. It only moves more of your money out.

distractors.label: Scan a QR code
distractors.explanation: Scanning a QR code is a way to pay. It is not a way to receive money, and it does not help here.

critical.title: You entered your UPI PIN to receive money
critical.explanation: A UPI PIN is only for sending money. It is never needed to receive money. If anyone says 'enter your PIN to receive', it is a scam. In real life, contact your bank's 24×7 helpline and report on 1930 or cybercrime.gov.in as soon as possible.
critical.reason: You entered a PIN on a collect request last time, so rehearse this next.

redFlags.textFragment: I'll buy your item right now at full price, no bargaining.
redFlags.label: Too easy a deal
redFlags.explanation: Scammers rush in with an easy deal so you stop checking.

redFlags.label: A request pulls money out
redFlags.explanation: A real payment to you does not need you to approve anything. A request asks you to pay.

redFlags.textFragment: enter your UPI PIN to receive the money
redFlags.label: PIN to receive
redFlags.explanation: A UPI PIN is only for sending money. You never need it to receive.

redFlags.textFragment: I can't talk on a call, only chat.
redFlags.label: Avoids a real conversation
redFlags.explanation: Scammers avoid calls because a voice is easier to check than a chat.

redFlags.textFragment: Do it urgently or I'll buy from someone else!
redFlags.label: Urgency pressure
redFlags.explanation: Pressure to act fast is designed to stop you from thinking.

redFlags.label: Unknown sender
redFlags.explanation: You do not know this person. Treat unknown senders with extra care.

hints.spot-flags: Scammers rush you with no-bargaining deals, refuse voice calls, and ask for a PIN to 'receive' money. Tap at least 3 suspicious phrases directly in the message bubble (avoid replying in chat).
hints.open-app: Never trust what a chat says about a payment—messages can lie about whether money is coming in or going out. Open {{app}} yourself from the Apps bar at the bottom to inspect the real request.
hints.decline-request: A UPI 'collect request' always pulls money OUT of your account when you approve it with your PIN; genuine incoming payments happen automatically. Tap the pending request in {{app}} and choose Decline.
hints.check-balance: Even after declining, verify your own ledger so you know for certain no unauthorised debit occurred. Tap Check balance & history on the {{app}} home screen.
hints.block-report: Scammers often resend collect requests hoping you slip up later. Open Security and help inside {{app}} to block the sender's UPI ID and submit a fraud report.
